Are There Really 200,000 Australians "Addicted" To Marijuana?

200,000 ADDICTED TO POT

For a more complete discussion of this issue see
Is Marijuana Addictive?
Perhaps Less So Than The Internet.
Analysis By Richard Cowan
and links

More than 2.7 million Australians smoke almost $5 billion worth of cannabis each year, with about 200,000 heavily dependent on the drug.
See
Australian Study Shows That Aussies Spend Far More On Marijuana Than On Wine.
Almost As Much As They Spend On Beer!
"Alcohol and marijuana seem to be substitutes, with cross-price elasticities."

But there is little awareness of cannabis addiction and governments spend almost nothing on helping people with drug-related problems.

Dr Jan Copeland, of the National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre, led a trial which found it was almost impossible for heavy users to quit.

"We are a nation that likes its pot," Dr Copeland said.

"There are millions of Australians who smoke the drug and use it quite responsibly, but there are a small percentage who become heavily dependent on cannabis."
(Marijuananews note: Obviously, this is not the prohibitionist party line. Most prohibitionists claim very high rates of "addiction" and never acknowledge – as this article does – that the overwhelming majority of marijuana smokers "use it quite responsibly.")

Of the 273 heavy users (who smoke it about eight times a day) in the study who wanted to quit, only 10 per cent who completed extensive counselling had been able to.

Adding other surveys' data to its own, Dr Copeland's team estimated 200,000 people were heavily dependent on cannabis.

The heavy users studied, who spent about a quarter of their income on the drug, became withdrawn and made cannabis the main focus of their lives.
(Marijuananews note: Marijuana prohibition has not helped them. In stead, it has just made their marijuana more expensive.)
General health problems and significant psychological problems were reported by 83 per cent; 69 percent of the sample were male, with an average age of 32, and most held full-time jobs.

(Marijuananews note: One of the problems that I have with this kind of study is that it never seems to occur to anyone that some of these people may be self-medicating. If they were taking prescription drugs, their "dependence" would be cited as proof that the drugs were working, even though many people report a variety of side-effects from pharmaceuticals that are much more severe than those reported here for cannabis.)
See
UK Victims of Tranquilizers Urge That "Far Safer" Medical Cannabis Be Made Available -- IoS
"More people died from benzodiazepine usage than from such drugs as heroin and cocaine."

They had begun smoking cannabis at 15, had done so for an average of almost 14 years.

(Marijuananews note: Australia seems to have a very high level of substance abuse in general.)

The team found that many suffered depression and blamed cannabis for poor concentration and memory, social isolation and lack of motivation.

(Marijuananews note: Even though most of them were employed…)
